findings.problem: Plain encargar means to order or to entrust, while to take care of is the meaning of the pronominal verb encargarse (de), so es does not match the prompt.
The hint shows the answer (me encargo), so it gives it away instead of only ruling out other answers such as cuidar or ocuparse.
findings.fix: hint: handle a task or be in charge of it; reflexive verb used with de

findings.problem: For this meaning the dictionary form is encargarse, and its present forms need the reflexive pronouns.
findings.fix: es: encargarse; grammar.present: yo me encargo, tú te encargas, él se encarga (irregular: false)

back.es: encargar: to order (goods), to commission, to put someone in charge of; only the pronominal encargarse (de) means to take care of / handle
back.example: Relax, I'll take care of everything.

note: The preterite encargué is only a spelling change, so irregular: false is correct.
